text:
incident-bot: ALERT: Elevated 5xx/error rate observed on inference-prod cluster us-west-2. Threshold 3% breached (current 18%). Paging oncall team. 

oncall-maya: I'm on it. pulling up dashboards and logs. rough ETA 5-10m to triage. :hourglass_flowing_sand:

sre-liz: seeing spike correlated to model-runner pods OOM/killed on node-gpu-7. Logs show repeated segfaults in libattention.so around KV-cache flush.

runtime-ryan: confirming. I see this in unit logs: ```E libc++abi: terminating with uncaught exception of type std::bad_alloc
[signal SIGSEGV: segmentation fault]
Backtrace: model_runner::attention::compute(...)``` Also kube shows CrashLoopBackOff for model-runner-92bb.

oncall-maya: customer impact? any 5xx spikes on gateway or per-tenant?

support-dave: Customer alerts: several clients (acct-45xx, acct-9xx) reported increased 502s and timeouts in the last 8 minutes. Support is replying with status update. No confirmed data exfiltration.

platform-ben: autoscaler didn't spin up new GPU nodes because node pool hit quota. We can temporarily route traffic to a smaller CPU-backed variant if runtime teams are okay.

ml-eva: We have a quantized 6B fallback (model-q6) that's CPU-friendly and known to be compatible. Quality is slightly lower but acceptable for emergency fallback.

runtime-ryan: Plan A: drain affected nodes, redeploy model-runner with patched allocator (hotpatch), and roll traffic back gradually. Plan B: enable fallback routing to model-q6 and scale gateway workers. Need approvals.

oncall-maya: agree. Prioritize customer availability. Start fallback routing + scale gateway. runtime-ryan, can you push hotpatch as low-risk canary after we stabilize?

runtime-ryan: yes. Preparing a minimal patch: change default KV flush frequency and add defensive null-check. Will build a canary image: `gcr.io/redwood/model-runner:hotfix-6923`.

sre-liz: I'll start draining pods on node-gpu-7 so we can repro on isolated environment. Command I'm running: ```kubectl cordon node-gpu-7 && kubectl drain node-gpu-7 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data```

platform-ben: increasing gateway replicas now and enabling routing rule to fallback model for requests >512 tokens. Doing `kubectl scale deployment/gateway --replicas=40` and hitting the API change: `POST /admin/routing` with payload `{ "route": "inference-prod", "fallback_model": "model-q6", "criteria": "all" }` (admins only).

oncall-maya: pagerduty-bot, escalate if errors persist beyond 20m.

pagerduty-bot: Escalation policy armed. Next level oncall will be notified in 20m if unresolved.

support-dave: notifying impacted customers: short note sent, linking status page. No compensation asks yet.

ml-eva: Quick note on perf: fallback model increases latency ~200ms on average but should reduce 5xx to near 0 for affected tenants. Good tradeoff.

runtime-ryan: canary image built and pushed. Starting a single canary deployment in us-west-2 with 2 pods pinned to node-gpu-canary. `kubectl apply -f canary-hotfix.yaml`

sre-liz: observed canary pods stable for last 90s. No segfaults so far. I'll let them run for 3 min before scaling.

oncall-maya: good. Meanwhile platform-ben, confirm fallback routing active and % traffic shifted.

platform-ben: fallback routing live. 70% traffic shifted to fallback model-q6, 30% to primary until canary validated. Gateway metrics show 5xx drop from 18% -> 3.2% in last 2m.

sre-liz: draining finished on node-gpu-7, restarted model-runner pods there on patched image; logs show no immediate crashes but memory footprint is higher by ~50MB. Monitoring.

runtime-ryan: running load test against patched nodes with synthetic traces. No segfaults in 10k requests. Pushing patch to prod in rolling fashion 10% -> 50% -> 100% with health checks.

oncall-maya: I'll update incident channel and incident status page. Please paste succinct rollback criteria here.

runtime-ryan: rollback criteria: if 5xx > 2% for 5 consecutive minutes OR crashloop rate per pod > 1 in 5m -> immediate rollback to previous image and re-enable fallback model routing.

ml-eva: also enabling continuous eval on a small prompt set to sanity-check output quality post-patch.

support-dave: support: tracking 6 customers who reported errors. Notifying them that fallback is active and we're doing a patch.

platform-ben: quota request submitted to cloud to add two additional GPU nodes as buffer once patch is validated. Might take 3-6m to provision.

runtime-ryan: rolling patch to 50% now. Health checks passing. No new segfaults in patched pods.

sre-liz: metrics: 5xx at 1.6% now. Latency slightly up where fallback model serving, as expected.

oncall-maya: good job. Who will be primary owner during postmortem? runtime-ryan + sre-liz + ml-eva?

runtime-ryan: I'll own the runtime/root cause and fix. sre-liz will own deployment/ops timeline. ml-eva will own model/regression checks.

incident-bot: INCIDENT UPDATE: 5xx rates dropped to 1.2%. Fallback routing still enabled. No active customer escalations.

support-dave: customers acknowledging status. One large tenant requested fine-grained logs; will coordinate with security and customer success.

oncall-maya: handing off to SRE oncall for monitoring window. I'm going offline in 10m. Keep channel updated with any regression.

sre-liz: taking handoff. I'll monitor for 1h and coordinate with runtime if needed. Setting temporary alert thresholds tighter.

runtime-ryan: followup items I will include in postmortem: stack traces pointer, suspect allocator path, KV-cache flush timing, and tests to catch this in CI.

ml-eva: I'll add a canary eval in CI that runs a short inference suite on quantized variants to detect regressions earlier.

platform-ben: provisioning complete for 2 extra GPUs, will keep them warm for 24h.

incident-bot: INCIDENT RESOLVED (partial): customer-facing availability restored via fallback. Root fix deployed to 100% with monitoring in place. Postmortem to follow.

oncall-maya: thanks team. Postmortem owner runtime-ryan; draft due EOD. Closing handoff. :white_check_mark:
